blocks.content: **Agents** is a catalog of every agent that has sent generations to Agent Observability. Each agent has one entry, and each entry lists the agent's versions. A version is created each time the agent declares a new `agent_version`. If the agent declares no version, each distinct system prompt counts as a version instead. This milestone reads the catalog for one agent, then opens that agent and reads its version history.
Open Agents and read what the catalog shows for each agent, then open one agent.
Go to **Observability** > **Agent** > **Agents** with a time range that covers the demo data.

Check the time range picker.

It governs the activity columns and the stats above the list. An agent appears when its observed lifetime overlaps the range, even if it sent nothing inside it; its activity columns then stay empty.

Look at the three risk counters above the list.

They flag agents worth a look: **anonymous buckets**, **stale** (last active more than 7 days before the end of the range), and **high churn** (many versions first seen in the range; the label shows the current threshold). Each counter is also a filter that narrows the list to the agents it flags.

Read the columns of the agents table.

Together they say which agents are active and which ones are spending. The eight demo agents carry a **Demo** badge.

In **Filter agent by name…**, type `data-analyst`.

The list narrows to `sigil.demo.data-analyst`.
Click the `sigil.demo.data-analyst` row to open the agent's page.
You read the catalog's columns and risk counters and opened one agent.
Read the agent's versions, its prompt and tools, and its quality scores.

Read the agent's header.

It summarizes what the catalog keeps for this agent and when the agent was first and last seen. The primary model, `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, is named beside the agent.

On **Overview**, read the version timeline and the **Version delta** panel below it.

The timeline lists every version with its label, a short hash, and when it was first seen. The one marked **Selected** is the version the rest of the page describes, and clicking an earlier version selects it instead.

The **Version delta** panel compares the selected version with the one before it. It counts the lines added and removed in the prompt and the tools added and removed. `sigil.demo.data-analyst` has one version, `1.0.0`, so the delta reads **Initial version** against an empty baseline.

Click **Prompts**.

It shows the selected version's system prompt in full, with its **Prompt tokens** and **Inventory context** counts, and **Analyze agent**, which produces prompt insights that summarize the prompt and point out patterns that may affect quality, latency, or cost.

Click **Tools**.

It lists the selected version's tools with the tokens each one's definition adds to every call: here `run_sql_query`, 20 tokens, with its description and input schema. Click a tool to read them.

Click **Quality**.

It charts the pass rate by evaluator for the latest scored versions, one bar per version, and the **previous version** and **next version** arrows step through them. This is where an evaluation score change between two versions shows.

You read what the catalog keeps for an agent and its versions. The version delta is on **Overview**, the prompt and tool footprint on **Prompts** and **Tools**, the pass rate on **Quality**, and the activity columns in **Agents**.

A second version appears when the agent declares a new `agent_version`, or changes its system prompt without declaring one. The **Version delta** then reads the difference between the two versions, and **Quality** shows one bar per version. A tool change alone is recorded in the version's tool snapshot and does not create a version.

Don't see `sigil.demo.data-analyst` in **Agents**? Check these in order:

1. The name filter is spelled `data-analyst`. Clear it to see the whole list.
2. The demo data is seeded on this stack. Demo agents carry a **Demo** badge; if none does, complete the Seed the demo data guide first.
3. None of the risk counters is active. An active counter filters the list to the agents it flags.

For the reference on versions and what to compare, refer to [Agent catalog](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/observe-and-act/agent-observability/observe-and-troubleshoot/agent-catalog/).
